newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austrian share rally runs out of steam.
newsitem.headline: Austrian share rally runs out of steam.

text.p: Austrian shares ended off the international pace on Thursday after selling pressure in the derivatives market wiped out a strong start and tipped the blue-chip ATX index 0.15 percent lower.
While German shares stormed to a record close, Austria's ATX finished 1.71 points at 1,130.96 -- well below the 1,142.06 session high. Overall 13 shares closed higher and eight lower.
"There was definitely a reluctance to allow the market to rise above 1,140 points," a trader said.

Sell orders spread from ATX futures, which touched a session high of 1,139 points before slipping to 1,130, to the cash market. Vienna airport company Flughafen Wien and engineering group VA Tech were among the most actively traded shares and the biggest decliners.
Flughafen slipped 1.9 percent to 516 schillings while VA Tech eased 1.6 percent to 1,703 schillings.
Some dealers remained optimistic that this week's upward trend would resume on Friday, however.
"If the international environment remains positive, we will certainly climb further," said one.

Among the leading gainers were ATX heavyweight EA-Generali and brewing stocks BBAG and Brau Union. BBAG and its unit Brau Union were boosted by news of the group's expansion into Romania and a forecast rise in 1996 pre-tax earnings.
EA-Generali added on 2.52 percent to 3,660 schillings.
BBAG closed 10 schillings up at 750, off a mid-session high of 760 and Brau Union finished four schillings up at 664, having rallied to 681 earlier.
The broad-based Vienna bourse index edged 1.36 points higher to 428.58.
